To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have prepared highly ordered multi-lamellar membranes of human RBCs, which are composed of domains of coiled-coil integral membrane proteins and liquid ordered and liquid disordered lipids.

we determined the molecular structure of human RBC membranes in a solid supported multi-lamellar membrane configuration by high resolution X-ray diffractions and found that these RBC membrane consist of nanometer-sized domains of integral co-iled-coil peptides and liquid ordered (lo), as well as liquid disordered (lo) lipids.

we have developed a method to prepare highly oriented stacks of RBC membranes and used this method to determine the molecular organization of the membranes, as well as to study how drugs interact with the membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods for the structural characterization of biological membranes.
the molecular structure of RBC membranes and the interaction of the membranes with drugs and other small molecules.
the structural organization of RBC membranes and the effect of aspirin on these membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RBC membrane consists of a complex mixture of different lipid and protein domains.
the RBC membrane consists of a lo and an ld domain, separated by coiled-coil domains.

the RBC membranes are patchy structures, consisting of nanometer sized, highly organized, liquid disordered domains of integral membrane peptides and liquid ordered domains of lipids with a fluidity gradient from the outer leaflet to the inner leaflet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined the structural properties of human red blood cells membranes and that we have shown that the drug aspirin has the capability to fluidify the membrane.
we have determined the molecular organization of the different domains in the RBC membrane.
the RBC membranes are composed of coiled-coil proteins, lo and ld lipids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular structure of RBC membranes can be determined from solid supported multi-lamellar membranes.
the RBC membrane is a patchy structure, where the lo domain is the most ordered domain.
the RBC membrane structure can be studied with high precision using XRD and that this approach is suitable to study interactions between RBC membranes and other molecules.
